_contract: The canonical owner of this pilot's COSTS. The ceiling is owned by authorization.json, which this file points at by PATH; scripts/pod/engineering_campaign_budget.py reads both and derives the session limit. The launcher carries no copy of any of it, because two places holding the same number is how one of them comes to be wrong. Read before each paid action. A rerun does NOT reset it and a replacement resource does NOT receive a fresh allocation.
_authorization_is_a_PATH_not_an_object: derive_budget.engineering_campaigns resolves `granted_utc` by reading this field as a relative path. An inline object leaves the date unresolved and the attribution `unknown`.
_the_ceiling_is_NOT_restated_here: It lives in authorization.json and nowhere else.
_inherits_nothing: This is a NEW campaign, distinct from the CLOSED batch-invariance root-cause diagnostic. That campaign's $0.7319 stays booked on its own record and is NOT charged here; the two ceilings are separate and neither funds the other.

subruns._rate_source: live securePrice re-queried immediately before creation
subruns.cost_basis: wall clock from pod creation to confirmed teardown x the live secure rate, plus container disk billed separately
subruns.stage_reached: prefix step 2 of 3 (WIDTH), before any causal scoring
subruns.failure: calib.reasoning_heavy@v2: artifacts/stage1/reasoning_heavy_v2/items.jsonl is missing. The remote payload staged ONE calibration mixture. The prefix uses TWO -- DEPTH and FFN on domain_balanced@v1, WIDTH on reasoning_heavy@v2 -- which is the exact non-uniformity a maintainer review had already corrected in the pilot module, and I staged for the uniform case anyway.
subruns.second_defect: the pod-side preflight PASSED. It runs the driver's --toy mode, which supplies `calibration_items` explicitly and therefore never resolves a profile at all, so the one check placed before the GPU work could not see the one input that was missing.
subruns.third_defect: the launcher fetched /workspace/out wholesale: 9.1 GiB of prefix checkpoints over a 0.72 MB/s uplink, with the pod still billing. Killed after ~15 min. The evidence is JSON; nothing on the dev box consumes those weights.
subruns.fourth_defect: 24 minutes of DEPTH and FFN produced NO recorded stage: the driver checkpoints `prefix` only after all three steps return, so a failure in the third discards the evidence of the first two.
subruns.repair: stage every profile the pilot's own steps name, derived from the pilot module rather than listed; add a --check-inputs mode that resolves the REAL profiles at $0 before the GPU work; exclude work/ from the fetch; persist each prefix step through on_step as it completes.
subruns.teardown: confirmed by provider query: pods 0, networkVolumes 0
subruns.artifacts_kept: every JSON, log and text record. The 9 partial .safetensors from the aborted transfer were removed: incomplete bytes from a failed run's intermediates, with no consumer.
